claims.statement: The slider's pointer target spans the full tap-target minimum even though the painted track is thinner.
The slider is reachable and operable from the keyboard through its native range control.
The thumb stays within the track at both ends of travel.
onChange fires for every movement and onChangeCommit fires once when the interaction ends, so a drag produces one persisted write rather than one per step.
aria-valuetext carries the formatted value, so assistive technology speaks the unit shown on screen.
The default marker is visually distinct from a step tick so the origin reads as a reference, not a stop.
A caller-supplied aria-labelledby is preserved rather than overwritten when the slider renders no label of its own.

component.purpose: Set a value along a continuous range, with the committed write separated from the live one.
component.title: Slider

states.description: Track, fill, thumb, and a formatted inline readout — the whole default surface.
Ticks mark every step and a taller notch marks the origin value, making drift visible.
Named marks label positions a bare number would not explain; the readout moves into a tooltip.
A host row owns the label and the control adopts it by id, rendering none of its own.
An unavailable slider keeps its value legible rather than hiding it.
